Hierarchical subsystems

Source: R/subsystems.R
sim_subsystem.Rd

A subsystem is an ordinary sim_model() whose external interface is declared with "inport" and "outport" blocks. Port numbers come from their index parameter. The subsystem is placed into a parent model with sim_add_block(parent, "subsystem", name, system = sub, params = ...).

sim_subsystem(name, params = list())

Arguments

name

Subsystem name.

params

Default parameters of the subsystem. Instance params override them.

Value

A sim_model.

Details

At compile time every subsystem instance is flattened into the parent: inner block b of instance s becomes block s/b. Each instance gets its own copy of the inner blocks, so instances never share state. A sim_param() reference inside the subsystem is resolved first in the instance's params, then in the parent's scope. The flattened model is mathematically identical to building the same blocks by hand.

sim_subsystem() is a convenience wrapper around sim_model().

Examples

# A first-order lag y' = (u - y) / tau, with inv_tau = 1 / tau.
lag <- sim_subsystem("lag", params = list(inv_tau = 1))
sim_add_block(lag, "inport", "u", index = 1)
sim_add_block(lag, "subtract", "e")
sim_add_block(lag, "gain", "k", gain = sim_param("inv_tau"))
sim_add_block(lag, "integrator", "y", initial = 0)
sim_add_block(lag, "outport", "out", index = 1)
sim_connect(lag, "u", "e", input = 1)
sim_connect(lag, "y", "e", input = 2)
sim_connect(lag, "e", "k")
sim_connect(lag, "k", "y")
sim_connect(lag, "y", "out")

m <- sim_model("two_lags")
sim_add_block(m, "step", "u", time = 0)
sim_add_block(m, "subsystem", "fast", system = lag, params = list(inv_tau = 10))
sim_add_block(m, "subsystem", "slow", system = lag, params = list(inv_tau = 1))
sim_connect(m, "u", "fast")
sim_connect(m, "u", "slow")
r <- sim_run(sim_compile(m), tspan = c(0, 3))
tail(sim_signal(r, c("fast", "slow")), 1)
#>        fast      slow
#> [201,]    1 0.9502129
